Reverse the order of a text's paragraphs or sentences

Source: R/doc-bench-condense.R
gr_reverse_text.Rd

Turns a document around, unit by unit, so a reader that goes through it in order meets the end first. Paragraphs are split at blank lines; sentences at a full stop, question mark or exclamation mark followed by white space. The units are joined as they were split, by a blank line or a space. gr_condensation_check() reads each planted document forwards and reversed with it.

Usage

gr_reverse_text(text, unit = c("paragraph", "sentence"))

Arguments

text

A single string.

unit

"paragraph" or "sentence".

Value

A single string.

See also

gr_condensation_check()

Other harness: gr_arm(), gr_condensation_check(), gr_qa_reference(), gr_scorer_answer(), hr_arm(), hr_benchmark(), hr_chain(), hr_contrast(), hr_drift_check(), hr_effort_check(), hr_effort_escalate(), hr_effort_event(), hr_effort_log(), hr_mdd(), hr_modules(), hr_reference(), hr_register(), hr_report(), hr_scorer(), hr_set(), hr_settings(), hr_skill(), hr_step(), hr_step_command(), hr_sweep(), hr_sweep_check()

Examples

gr_reverse_text("First part.\n\nSecond part.\n\nThird part.")
#> [1] "Third part.\n\nSecond part.\n\nFirst part."
gr_reverse_text("One. Two. Three.", unit = "sentence")
#> [1] "Three. Two. One."
